source: CDC Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule, 2026; AAP 2026 Immunization Schedule policy statement (Pediatrics)
notes_to_renderer: All dose ages assume term infant with no contraindications. Premature/medical exceptions defer to pediatrician.
RSV strategy in 2026 is either maternal RSVpreF vaccine in pregnancy OR infant nirsevimab/clesrovimab dosing in first RSV season — not both. Confirm which path the OB/peds team chose.
Influenza begins at 6 months and is annual.
MMR, Varicella, HepA standardly given at the 12-month well visit (the bridge into year 2).

severity_thresholds.call_now: anaphylaxis (rare): facial swelling, breathing difficulty, hypotonia

doses.notes: Two formulations: RV5 (RotaTeq) is a 3-dose series at 2/4/6 mo; RV1 (Rotarix) is a 2-dose series at 2/4 mo. First dose must be given by 14 weeks 6 days; series complete by 8 mo 0 days.

severity_thresholds.call_within_24h: fever >104°F, swelling extending past joint, persistent crying >3h, hypotonic-hyporesponsive episode

doses.notes: PCV20 is approved for the full series; PCV15 also acceptable. Either covers serotypes responsible for most invasive pneumococcal disease in young children.

Schedule depends on product (Moderna vs. Pfizer-BioNTech) and whether infant has had prior doses. As of 2026 the AAP and CDC schedules diverged on COVID-19 routine recommendation; check both with your pediatrician.

doses.conditional: Only if RV5 (RotaTeq) product is in use; RV1 (Rotarix) ends at 2 doses.

doses.age: 6 months (if PRP-T product) — may be omitted if PRP-OMP product
doses.notes: PRP-OMP Hib (PedvaxHIB) is a 2-dose primary series (2 mo, 4 mo) plus booster; PRP-T (ActHIB, Hiberix) is a 3-dose primary series.
First flu season: 2 doses 4 weeks apart if first time receiving flu vaccine. Subsequent seasons: 1 dose annually.

doses.age: 4 weeks after first flu dose (first season only)
doses.notes: Only required for first flu season.

doses.age: Birth–8 months entering first RSV season (typically Oct–Mar)
doses.notes: Skip if mother received RSVpreF (Abrysvo) in pregnancy at ≥32 weeks gestation and infant born ≥14 days after maternal vaccination. Clesrovimab is a newer 2024-approved alternative.
Crosses into year 2 but typically given at 12-month well visit. Mild rash and fever 7–12 days post-vaccine is common (not contagious).
